subject: MAP priorities and procurement hold — proposed re-prioritization and risk log
messages:
From: Danielle Park <dpark@solstice.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP update + procurement timing

Marcus / Laura —

Quick update from our procurement team: they’ve kicked the legal review into an additional internal cycle to validate data residency and SLA flows. That review likely pushes our internal sign-off by ~2 weeks unless we can compress one of the other steps in the MAP.

Can you confirm the absolute minimal evaluation window you need to complete the acceptance checklist? Current asks from procurement are: SOC2 evidence, sample keystore config, and a short latency report for our baseline 5k qps test. I attached the updated SOQ for reference.

If we need to shift the target close date, we’d like a short, prioritized MAP that highlights only the must-haves for go/no-go and what can be deferred post-signature.

Proposed next steps from my side:
- Procurement will attempt to get the second-level review completed by May 14th if we can provide the keystore and a short exec summary.
- I’ll escalate to our engineering lead for the latency gating request.

Thanks — can we discuss in a quick 20-min call tomorrow?

—Danielle
Danielle Park
Head of Data Platform, Solstice AI
Danielle.Park@solstice.ai
Attachment: SOQ_v2.pdf (application/pdf, 142KB)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <dpark@solstice.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP update + procurement timing

Danielle —

Thanks for the heads up and for attaching the SOQ. I appreciate the timeline clarity. Short answers up front: we can compress the evaluation window to as short as 5 business days for core acceptance criteria if Solstice agrees to two concessions: (1) run the baseline latency test within the first 48 hours of the window and (2) sign an evaluation addendum that allows us to enable aggressive prefix cache warming during the eval phase.

Risk log entries (high level):
- Risk A (procurement gating): Additional legal review -> possible 10–14 day slip to signature. Mitigation: supply keystore doc + executive summary (we can draft). Owner: Solstice / Marcus.
- Risk B (evaluation exposure): If production-like traffic not available, evaluation may under-report tail latency. Mitigation: Redwood to provide a dedicated test pool and a synthetic 5k qps harness. Owner: Redwood / Soojin.
- Risk C (contract redlines): SLA reductions requested by Solstice -> require sales escalation. Mitigation: hold current rate card and defer SLA optimization to post-signature. Owner: Marcus / Sales Leadership.

Proposed re-baseline (minimal MAP for signature):
1) May 6–10: Compressed evaluation (5 business days) — Redwood provides test harness, Solstice provides traffic profile.
2) May 11: Internal procurement final review window (Solstice) — target internal approval.
3) May 12–14: DocuSign routing + exec signoff.
4) May 15: Go-live/turn-on in dedicated pool (soft launch) — feature flags on.

If procurement cannot hit May 11, fallback is to slip the close date to May 25. That is our conservative cap; beyond that we need to re-evaluate quarterly capacity planning.

I’ve attached a quick schedule (evaluation-schedule.xlsx) — short timeline, owners, and acceptance checklist.

Happy to jump on a 20-min call tomorrow at 10am PT. Laura / Soojin — flagging this for procurement/eng alignment and any comments on the mitigation wording.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
Attachment: evaluation-schedule.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 28KB)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 19:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP update + procurement timing

Marcus / Soojin —

Please escalate this to the account exec (I’ll loop them). We should approve a one-week grace on the close if procurement is genuinely reviewing for residency and not asking for additional product guarantees. Also ask Legal to prepare a one-page exec summary that addresses the keystore/KMS model and the SOC2 artifact list. That doc is what procurement will push through their review faster.

If you get any ask that materially changes SLA language, stop negotiations and route to me + finance. We cannot take open-ended SLA exposure for this deal without exec approval.

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success & GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <dpark@solstice.ai>, Procurement <procurement@solstice.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Sales Leadership <sales_leadership@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation note — MAP re-prioritization request (DEAL-12873)

Danielle / procurement team —

Following our thread, Redwood is prepared to execute the compressed MAP and provide a gated evaluation pool as described. Per Laura’s note, we’ll hold on any SLA language concessions until finance + sales leadership confirm. For procurement: please accept the attached keystore configuration (see SOQ_v2.pdf) and provide a tentative internal sign-off date; if Solstice can commit to May 11 for the procurement decision, we will hold the May 15 soft-launch slot.

If the procurement committee requires more time, we propose the following escalation path to avoid indefinite slip:
- Week 0 (current): accept keystore doc and confirm short eval window.
- Week 1 (grace): Redwood reserves the current price and capacity for one week beyond the originally planned close date; Finance to approve hold.
- Week 2+: If no sign-off after one-week grace, Sales leadership to re-evaluate capacity commit and pricing.

Action items:
- Danielle: confirm whether procurement can commit to May 11 (reply here).
- Soojin: stand up dedicated test pool on May 6 and share access.
- Laura: confirm finance approval for the one-week hold by EOD Monday.
- Marcus: prepare one-page exec summary for procurement (attached link to HubSpot + DocuSign placeholder).

Thanks — escalating so execs have visibility.
